 What Micron’s Record Margin Means For Your Shares
 November 19th, 2026 · by Trefis Team MU YTD +142.1% SPY YTD +5.8% QQQ YTD +5.4% Analyze MU → Today’s big story: Could Anthropic Stock Fall 25%? 
 Micron Technology (MU) closed at $705.27 on Wednesday, Nov 18. That is 41.9% below its high close of $1,213.56 on June 25. Yet the memory chip maker’s latest reported quarter was the best in its history. Most coverage looks at the demand for memory that AI brings. This article looks at the memory cycle instead.
 The measure is gross margin. It is the share of sales left after the direct cost of making the chips. In the quarter ended Sept 3, 2026, Micron kept 86.8% of its sales this way. That is the highest of all 107 quarters in our data since 2000. The best before 2025 was 61.0%, in 2018.
 History is not kind to a margin peak. Micron had 8 completed gross-margin peaks from 2000 to 2021. After all 8, the stock was lower 12 months later. It also trailed the S&P 500 all 8 times. The stock’s median 12-month change was a fall of 34.7%. So has the cycle peaked? The margin peak is not confirmed yet. But the stock is already falling the way it did before past peaks.
 Image from Pixabay 
 What did Micron stock do after each past margin peak?
 The falls were deep even when the year ended well. Within 12 months of each peak, the stock’s deepest drop had a median of 45.3%. Over the same windows, the S&P 500 had a median change of 0.9%. The S&P 500 also fell after the 2000, 2002 and 2021 peaks. In the other five windows it rose, so the pain came from the memory cycle.
 Falls of that size are hard to sit through. Holding on is easier when your portfolio falls less than the market. For every dollar its benchmark lost, the Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio lost about 81 cents on average. See the HQ record .

A peak is a quarter whose gross margin is at least as high as the four quarters before it and the four after it. Each window starts at the close on the quarter’s last day. The deepest fall is the lowest close in the window, compared with the start.
 The mildest case was 2010. The stock slipped 0.9% while the S&P 500 rose 17.9%. The worst was 2002, with a fall of 75.1%. That peak was weak, at a margin of only 22.1%. Eight cases is a small sample, so we read the record as a pattern, not a rule.
 Did the stock fall before the margin did?
 Yes, every time. At the end of each of the 8 peak quarters, the stock was already below its high close of the prior year. The median gap was 17.3%. Buyers left before the margin turned.
 The same order shows up now. At the Sept 3 close, the last day of the record quarter, Micron was 21.0% below its June 25 high. Since that close it has fallen another 26.4%. In past cycles, the margin four quarters after a peak was lower by a median 27.5 percentage points.
 What could make this cycle different?
 The record quarter is not a confirmed peak. No later quarter has been reported yet. If the next margin is higher still, the old pattern does not yet apply.
 Analysts expect a lot more growth. Their average estimate for fiscal 2027 revenue is $278.0 billion. That is 108.8% above fiscal 2026. Their average earnings estimate for the same year, which ends in Sept 2027, is $175.61 a share. On that estimate, Micron trades at 4.0 times this fiscal year’s expected profit. On fiscal 2026’s reported profit, it trades at 9.5 times.
 The cash is real too. In the record quarter, Micron’s business brought in $44.0 billion of operating cash. After spending on plants and equipment, $32.9 billion was left. That money is called free cash flow.
 Our earlier piece, Why Micron’s Cheap P/E Has Often Meant A Peak, looks at the same cycle through the price-to-earnings ratio.
 How have other storage stocks and Nvidia moved?
 Micron and Nvidia both fell this week. Between the Friday, Nov 13 close and the Nov 18 close, Micron lost 9.4% of its value. Nvidia fell 7.3% over the same days.
 Two other data storage makers also earn high margins while their shares slide.
 SanDisk kept 85.0% of sales as gross profit in the quarter ended Oct 2. Its stock is 66.8% below its June 25 high.
 Western Digital had a gross margin of 57.8% in the same quarter. Its stock is 61.4% below its June 18 high.
 Nvidia is 36.9% below its Oct 6 high close.
 This piece is part of our AI story . Several AI stocks are well off their highs at the same time. Our look at Do Nvidia, Alphabet, Meta Drops Hurt Your Index Fund? covers the wider picture.
 What would bring Micron’s buyers back?
 A next quarter with a higher margin would show the peak is not here yet. A lower one would match the old pattern. Our data does not show what caused this week’s fall.
 Our read: the record margin is real, but in every past cycle the stock did not wait for the margin to turn. If Micron has grown into a big part of your account, it helps to decide now when and how much you would sell.
